pluralRules.one-if-1: The count takes the 'one' form when it is exactly 1, and 'other' in every other case, zero included.
pluralRules.pt-cardinal-cldr46: CLDR 46 Portuguese cardinal rule for canonical numeric counts (no compact exponent or preserved trailing decimal zeros): the absolute integer part 0 or 1 takes one; other nonzero integral multiples of 1000000 take many; all other counts take other.
pluralRules.zh-cardinal-cldr46: CLDR 46 Chinese cardinal rule: every count takes other; the language has no grammatical number.
pluralRules.he-cardinal-cldr46: CLDR 46 Hebrew cardinal rule for canonical numeric counts (no compact exponent or preserved trailing decimal zeros): the absolute integer part 1 with no fraction, or 0 with a fraction, takes one; the absolute integer part 2 with no fraction takes two; every other count takes other, 20 and 100 included.

pluralRulesNote: A locale whose pluralRule is null has no rule pinned yet, and every runtime refuses it rather than borrowing another locale's -- English and Portuguese disagree about zero, and a borrowed rule reads as fluent, confident, wrong grammar to anyone who does not speak the language. Pinning a rule means transcribing it from a CLDR release and naming it here, so all three runtimes select the same form for the same count.
numberFormatNote: Separators are declared here rather than read from each runtime's own locale database. ICU data differs between engines and the ICU version behind a runtime changes between releases; a table that lives in one place is the only way the same number reaches every reader identically.
